clue.text: Lag behind, right in the rear

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for right is placed inside the word for the rear

parts.note: the tail is the rear end of something

explanation.surface: A straggler is told off for trailing at the back of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag behind is to follow at the back, as a straggler does in a race.

clue.text: Dexterous, but for a doctor there's nothing to it

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims surgery is easy for a doctor, nothing to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone skilful and quick with their hands or wits.

clue.text: Middle west ground to be avoided

indicators.note: Middle asks for the central letters of the word west, dropping its outer letters

parts.note: food that has been chewed has been ground between the teeth

explanation.surface: A stretch of the American Midwest is said to be land best kept away from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle west' looks like the American region, but it means the middle letters of WEST, which are ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to shun or deliberately keep clear of it.

clue.text: May be charged with assault

explanation.surface: A suspect may face a charge of assault.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, assault and battery go together; a battery is also charged with electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell storing electricity is recharged, and battery is the legal term for unlawful physical attack.

clue.text: Water a mother's beer

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother, here with its possessive s
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone waters down their mother's beer.
explanation.walkthrough: ADAM'S ALE is an old jocular name for plain water, as drunk by the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous old expression for drinking water.

clue.text: One who may be troubled with heat burns?

definitions.text: One who may be troubled with heat burns?

parts.words: One who may be troubled with heat burns?
parts.note: heat burns reads like indigestion, but means sunburn suffered by someone lying out in strong sunshine

explanation.surface: A person suffering from heartburn-like complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat burns' suggests the digestive complaint heartburn; here it is the skin burnt by lying in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out to tan risks being burnt by the sun's heat.

clue.text: Skilled worker and master in rebuilding

indicators.note: rebuilding means the letters of and master are rearranged into a new structure

explanation.surface: A craftsman and a master builder work together on a reconstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a craftsman such as a plumber or electrician.

clue.text: Head leaves the platform in reproach

indicators.note: Head leaves says the first letter departs from the word for the platform

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: A leader steps off the stage amid criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head leaves' removes P, the first letter of PODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is the disgrace or general hatred that follows shameful conduct, close to reproach.

clue.text: Rogue quietly abandoned swindle

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter for quietly is dropped from the word for rogue

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal or rogue
P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A crook quietly gives up on a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme or fraud.

clue.text: A wounding glance, maybe

parts.note: glance means a glancing blow, so this is a bullet that bounces off a surface and wounds someone

explanation.surface: A cutting look exchanged between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'wounding glance' sounds like a hurtful look; it is a shot glancing off a wall and hitting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile glancing off a surface and flying on can injure a bystander.

clue.text: Obtain pass

explanation.surface: Get hold of a ticket to go past.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to acquire it, and to call in on or go past someone is another sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Store between 180 and 270 degrees

parts.note: on a compass, 180 degrees is due south, S
between X and Y is read as from X to Y, so and gives TO
270 degrees on a compass is due west, W

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's stock sits at some odd angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between 180 and 270 degrees' is the compass sector from South to West: S TO W.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow goods is to pack them away, which is what storing means.

clue.text: Pack divisions into defensive positions

parts.note: to ram is to pack something tightly
parts are sections or divisions

explanation.surface: Army units are packed into fortified lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramparts are the earth walls of a fortification, defended by troops.

clue.text: Talked with opposite number

parts.note: the converse of something is its opposite
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a number

explanation.surface: Two people spoke to the person sitting across the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To have conversed is to have spoken in conversation.

clue.text: Start of theatre in the round, a building

indicators.note: in tells us the opening letter goes inside the words round plus a

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Start of picks the first letter of theatre

explanation.surface: Theatre performed in the round needs a suitable building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of theatre' is T, which goes inside ROUND A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, often domed.

clue.text: Elated, having got a rise

explanation.surface: Thrilled after getting a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits lifted high mean joy, and something raised up has literally been hoisted.

clue.text: Hidden — but not from a gunman?

explanation.surface: Someone concealed, but not safely out of a gunman's sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Being under cover hides you, yet being held at gunpoint is also this word: covered by a gunman, not from one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under cover is concealed, and a gunman aiming at someone has them in his sights.

clue.text: It's unusual to hear in broadcasting

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of to hear in are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: It's rare to hear something in a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme being transmitted live is going out over the airwaves.

clue.text: Distressed by an unknown number of debts?

parts.note: taken as written
in algebra X stands for an unknown quantity
IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: Someone worried by owing an uncertain number of loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Worried and uneasy both describe a troubled state of mind.

clue.text: I've turned to lemon squash — a bad sign

indicators.note: turned means the letters of I've are twisted round into a new order
squash means the letters of lemon are crushed into a different shape

explanation.surface: Someone has switched to drinking lemon squash, a worrying development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges IVE to EVI, and 'squash' rearranges LEMON to LOMEN; lemon squash is a British fruit cordial.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen of evil is a portent foretelling misfortune.

clue.text: Indicate the victim

explanation.surface: Pointing out who is to be the target.
explanation.definitionFit: To point something out is to signal it, and a target of a con man is his dupe.

clue.text: Change direction and gear

explanation.surface: A sailor turns and changes gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing boats turn by going about into the wind, and riding equipment for horses is also called by this name.

clue.text: Relation puts us in the money

indicators.note: in tells us the word us is placed inside the word for money

parts.note: coin is money in metal form
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative cuts us in on the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' is a link; 'in' places US inside COIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of an uncle or aunt.

clue.text: Way an individual put on weight

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
one is a single person

explanation.surface: A diet that someone abandoned so they gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A STONE is a British unit of body weight equal to 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone is a traditional British measure of mass, fourteen pounds.

clue.text: Quietly mention favour

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly
to refer to something is to mention it

explanation.surface: Someone quietly brings up a favour they are owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one option is to like it better than the others.

clue.text: Unfairness in the value of shares

parts.note: taken as written
equity is the value of shareholders' stake in a company

explanation.surface: An injustice found in share valuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustice and unfairness both mean a lack of even-handed treatment.

clue.text: Reduced numbers, we infer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Reduced numbers, we infer (5)'. 'we infer' holds the answer's letters only with IN taken out, but no clue word signals that removal; no source found for the parse.

clue.text: Weapons unit — one seen in battle

indicators.note: seen in tells us the first pieces are placed inside the name of the battle

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was a First World War battle
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A weapons unit is spotted in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons is a Belgian town where British forces fought in 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: Munitions are military armaments and ammunition.
